frontmatter_target.title: Auditing-shared Skill-binding convention for execution-phase agents

body_target_sections: Context — auditing-shared as cross-cutting helper-home per ADR-0031; this feature's execution-side agents materially depend on multiple auditing-shared scripts; existing planning-side agents invoke single scripts via Bash without binding the SKILL.md

Decision — execution-side agents that materially depend on multiple auditing-shared scripts MAY bind auditing-shared in their skills: field (loading SKILL.md as context) in addition to invoking scripts via Bash. Planning-side agents that invoke a single script via Bash do not need the binding. The convention is OPT-IN for cross-cutting helper-home skills; not mandatory.

Validation evidence — 4 agents in this feature bind auditing-shared (execute-orchestrator, execute-task-quality-handler, execute-phase-quality-reviewer, execute-finalize-reconciler) per cc-design.md (reviewer_verdict=approved)

Consequences — Positive: shared conceptual model available to agents materially depending on multiple scripts. Negative: context-window cost for agents loading the SKILL.md. Forward implications: future features authoring new audit-touching agents have ADR-0035 to cite for the binding decision.

Alternatives considered — Alt 1: fold into ADR-0032 (rejected: ADR-0032 already at 5 changes; muddles framing). Alt 2: defer to a follow-on conventions feature (rejected: deviation already in play in this feature; needs ratification now per ADR-0029).
Notes — Pairs with ADR-0031 (canonical-helper-home) — ADR-0031 defines where the shared scripts live; ADR-0035 defines how downstream agents bind to them.
